messages:
arjun: Heads up — after landing PR that enables torch.compile + prime CUDA graph on first forward, we're seeing regressed p99 on seqlen 128 workloads (~20-30ms). profiler attached.
jess: ugh. is this only when kv cache is warm?
arjun: good q. repro shows cold KV path ok. perf jumps when capture happens with non-zero KV offsets (i.e., after decoding a few tokens). suspect capture cached kernels for shorter seqlens and then input seqlen changes -> wrong autotune path.
kevin: can you paste the perf counters? also which cudnn/cuda/cuBlas versions?
arjun: paste: ```PERF: kernel_select=fast_matmul_v2 (chosen_by_autotune) seqlen=32 -> 16ms. Later seqlen=128 picks fallback=matmul_generic -> 46ms. env: CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.1```
sophie: maybe torch.compile graph capture pins shapes and we never retrigger autotune when seqlen distribution shifts. we saw similar with batching heuristics
mike: if capture uses cached kernel handles, it won't consult kernel selector on replay. need a hook to re-run selector when KV cache length changes.
perf-bot: created perf-issue #3217 linking traces: https://redwood/infra/perf/3217 :warning:
jess: quick mitigation: disable graph capture for decode loop, or force uncapture on KV length change. which is easier?
arjun: disabling capture reduces p99 back to baseline. but increases cpu overhead. proposing: add capture guard that includes KV_offset in capture key so different cache lengths map to different captures.
kevin: can we instead set a fallback to trigger autotune when observed seqlen>threshold? cheaper than multiple captures.
sophie: agree. autotune trigger + small fallback capture ttl may be best. Also need integration test.
mike: I'll take a patch to add KV_len into capture key. arjun can you open PR with perf numbers?
arjun: done, PR#8421 created. will add regression test and flags. thanks :thumbsup:
